tasks_completed.description: #5b — Extract web table renderer to MarkdownTableWeb.tsx (Option iii render-prop) and wrap <td>/<th> in single parent <Text> with correct styles
tasks_completed.rationale: Cycle 1's regression: <RenderSpans> placed directly inside web <td>/<th> without parent <Text> caused RNW to render each sibling <Text> as block-level, stacking spans vertically. Native path at MarkdownView.tsx:470-472 (header) + 478-480 (body) wraps <RenderSpans> in <Text style={tableHeaderText|tableCellText}>. Cycle 5 mirrors this proven pattern in the web path. Architecture chosen: render-prop (Option iii from BA spec REV-6 — codex-canonical) — new sibling MarkdownTableWeb.tsx imports nothing from MarkdownView.tsx (no circular import); MarkdownView.tsx passes RenderSpans + tableHeaderTextStyle + tableCellTextStyle as props. Result: MarkdownView.tsx shrinks from 819 to 755 lines (under 800-line cap); zero cap-waiver needed; native path remains untouched.
tasks_completed.structural_check_evidence: Live DOM inspection on dev.life-ai.app/dev/codex-render-fixtures: every <td> and <th> now contains exactly one <div dir="auto"> child (the React Native Web Text element) with display: inline. Spans are children of the wrapper div and flow inline. This is the exact pattern that the native path uses at MarkdownView.tsx:478-482 (which already worked correctly).

git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Cycle 1 BA directed dev to route table cell strings through parseMarkdownSpans at render time. Dev added the parser call faithfully but missed that the JSX tree needed to mirror the native path's parent <Text> wrapper to establish RNW inline text-flow context.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: L2 structural change: extracted web table renderer to a sibling file via render-prop pattern (no circular import), and wrapped <RenderSpans> in single parent <Text style={tableHeaderText|tableCellText}> for both <td> and <th>. This mirrors the proven native pattern at MarkdownView.tsx:470-482 verbatim. RNW Text wrapper establishes inline text-flow context; child spans flow horizontally instead of stacking vertically.

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Inline-fix (Option i, ~10 lines) was rejected by BA because MarkdownView.tsx is at 819 > 800-line cap and an inline fix would exceed the cap further. BA selected Option iii render-prop extraction (REV-6) which moves ~50 lines of web-table code OUT of MarkdownView.tsx into the new sibling, plus adds JSX wrapping <Text> + render-prop props plumbing. Total new file is 214 lines because the project quality gate caps functions at 30 lines; the original 50-line web-table block had to be split into 8 smaller function components (WebTableCell, WebTableHeaderCell, WebTableRow, WebTableHead, WebTableBody, WebTableInner, RenderTableBlockWeb, useTableStyles) to satisfy the gate. Each component is a thin wrapper preserving the original logic verbatim. MarkdownView.tsx's net delta is -64 lines (819→755), bringing it under cap. Overall solution achieves the spec goal: structural fix lands, no cap-waiver needed.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed the render-prop architecture is sound: (1) Calling RenderSpans as a plain function vs JSX-element is NOT semantically problematic in this case because RenderSpans has no top-level hooks — but recommended aliasing as `const RenderSpans = props.renderSpans;` and JSX-rendering it for future-proofing if RenderSpans ever gains hooks. ADOPTED. (2) useUnistyles in sibling file: no concern — context propagates by React tree, not file location. ADOPTED. (3) Empty-cell fallback row[colIndex] ?? '': preserve. ADOPTED. (4) Last-column-no-borderRight for both <td> and <th>: preserve. ADOPTED. (5) ScrollView container CSS (overflowX:auto, width:fit-content, maxWidth:min(100%, calc(100vw-32px))): preserve exactly. ADOPTED. (6) `any` style typing: acceptable matching existing baseStyle?: any pragma. ADOPTED. (7) Add `selectable={props.selectable}` to wrapper <Text>: ADOPTED. (8) Preserve @ts-ignore on raw <div>/<table>: ADOPTED. (9) Import React and MarkdownSpan type: ADOPTED.
